reforms.description: The government should re-examine measures to stimulate business R&D, including the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit. The text recommends exploring alternative approaches such as more closely targeting tax credits on R&D undertaken by new firms rather than small firms and on incremental R&D, while being careful to minimize deadweight costs.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Reforming R&D tax credits to target new firms and incremental R&D more effectively can reduce deadweight costs and improve the allocation of innovation incentives, supporting productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'Measures to stimulate business R&D should be re-examined' and recommends exploring alternative approaches, indicating this is a policy recommendation rather than an implemented reform.
reforms.importance_rationale: This represents a significant but not structural reform to an existing major innovation instrument (SR&ED). The recommendation to retarget the tax credit from small firms to new firms and incremental R&D could meaningfully improve innovation incentives, though implementation remains uncertain.
reforms.source_quote: An alternative approach of more closely targeting tax credits on R&D undertaken by new firms rather than small firms perse and on incremental R&D could be explored. But such tax credits need to be carefully designed in order to bring forth new innovation whilst minimising deadweight costs.

reforms.description: The government should develop a clearly articulated and integrated national science and technology policy to steer decisions in public research. The text emphasizes that more research into understanding the innovation process may provide better value than launching costly new initiatives based on weak analytical underpinnings.
reforms.component_name: National Science and Technology Policy Framework
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: A coherent national science and technology policy can improve the allocation of public research funding and enhance the productivity of public R&D investments, supporting long-term productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'A clearly articulated and integrated national science and technology policy to steer decisions in public research is also needed,' indicating a policy recommendation rather than an implemented reform.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a significant governance reform that would establish a coherent framework for public research funding decisions. However, it is presented as a recommendation rather than an adopted policy, and its scope and depth remain undefined.
reforms.source_quote: A clearly articulated and integrated national science and technology policy to steer decisions in public research is also needed.

reforms.description: The government should remove the tax advantage afforded to Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations (LSVCCs) to enable the venture capital market to function more effectively in supporting innovation. The text notes that LSVCCs have lowered the average quality of venture capital deals and crowded out other venture capital funds.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Removing tax distortions in the venture capital market will improve capital allocation to higher-quality innovation projects and reduce crowding-out effects, supporting more efficient innovation financing.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'The tax advantage afforded to the LSVCCs should be removed,' indicating a policy recommendation rather than an implemented reform.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a significant but targeted reform to remove a specific tax distortion in the venture capital market. It addresses a clear market failure (crowding-out and quality degradation) but is narrower in scope than a system-wide innovation policy overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: The tax advantage afforded to the LSVCCs should be removed so as to enable the venture capital market to play its role in innovation more effectively.

reforms.description: Canada's innovation strategy focuses on knowledge, skills, the innovation environment and community-based innovation, with emphasis on public R&D governance through an integrated strategy and re-examination of generous tax credits for business R&D.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Re-examination of R&D tax credits aims to optimize public support for private-sector innovation and improve allocative efficiency of innovation funding.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'generous tax credits for business R&D should be re-examined' as part of the country's innovation strategy focus.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant policy review of an existing major instrument (business R&D tax credits) that could reshape how Canada supports private-sector innovation, though the text does not specify concrete changes yet.
reforms.source_quote: Public R&D needs to be governed by an integrated strategy, while generous tax credits for business R&D should be re-examined.

reforms.description: Canada's innovation strategy emphasizes more attention to commercialisation of R&D, recognizing the importance of translating research into market applications.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhanced focus on commercialisation of R&D strengthens the translation of public research into private-sector innovation and productivity gains.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'More attention is being paid to commercialisation of R&D' as part of the country's innovation strategy.
reforms.importance_rationale: A strategic shift in innovation policy focus towards commercialisation, reflecting recognition that knowledge transfer is critical to innovation diffusion and economic returns.
reforms.source_quote: More attention is being paid to commercialisation of R&D.

reforms.description: The survey recommends removal of the tax advantage provided to Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital (LSVC) corporations to improve venture capital market performance.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Removing inefficient tax subsidies to LSVC corporations would improve capital allocation efficiency in the venture capital market and reduce deadweight loss.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'the venture capital market would perform better if the tax advantage provided to Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital corporations were removed' as a policy recommendation.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted reform of an existing tax instrument affecting venture capital financing for innovative firms; significant for startup ecosystem efficiency but narrower in scope than system-wide changes.
reforms.source_quote: the venture capital market would perform better if the tax advantage provided to Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital corporations were removed.

reforms.description: Canada's innovation strategy, organised into four key areas (knowledge performance, skills performance, innovation environment, and community-based innovation), with specific targets by 2010 including ranking among the top five countries in R&D performance, doubling government R&D investment, and developing at least 10 internationally recognised technology clusters.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The strategy aims to increase public and private R&D investment, develop skilled labour, and create innovation clusters, all of which support productivity growth and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The strategy was organised into four key areas with goals and targets, and a 2004 assessment of progress was commissioned from the Conference Board of Canada.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a comprehensive, system-wide innovation strategy with multiple pillars (knowledge, skills, environment, clusters) and ambitious targets spanning the decade to 2010. It represents a major structural commitment to innovation policy across multiple dimensions.
reforms.source_quote: Canada's innovation strategy has been organised into four key areas each with goals and specific targets. These are set out below, along with the first assessment, in 2004, of progress towards meeting them.

reforms.description: The government increased spending on science and technology activities by almost 40% in real terms over the past decade, allocating CAD 9 billion (around 0.7% of GDP) to science and technology in 2004.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D spending builds the knowledge base and research capacity, which are important precursors to innovation and productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The government increased its spending on science and technology activities by almost 40% in real terms over the past decade, and in 2004 allocated CAD 9 billion.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant increase in public R&D funding (40% in real terms over a decade) represents a meaningful expansion of the research base, though it is presented as an ongoing trend rather than a discrete policy reform.
reforms.source_quote: The government increased its spending on science and technology activities by almost 40% in real terms over the past decade, and in 2004 allocated CAD 9 billion (around 0.7% of GDP) to it.

reforms.description: The government's National Science Advisor proposed a framework for evaluating and prioritising proposals for major science investments and overseeing the management of those projects, emphasising the need for a clearly articulated, integrated national science and technology policy.
reforms.package_name: National Science and Technology Policy Framework
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: A more coordinated and strategic framework for major science investments improves allocative efficiency and ensures public R&D resources are directed toward high-impact projects.
reforms.status_evidence: The National Science Advisor proposed a framework and sought comments on it during the course of 2005. The text states this strategic step 'remains to be taken'.
reforms.importance_rationale: A proposed framework for evaluating and prioritising major science investments represents a significant governance reform that would align Canada with OECD best practice, though it had not yet been implemented at the time of writing.
reforms.source_quote: The government's National Science Advisor proposed a framework for evaluating and prioritising proposals for major science investments and overseeing the management of those projects once approved and sought comments on it during the course of 2005.

reforms.description: The federal government provides the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Investment Tax Credit to encourage private-sector R&D, with differentiated credit rates and refundability rates based on business type and income thresholds. Tax expenditures were estimated at CAD 2.5 billion in 2005.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Tax credits can incentivise private R&D and innovation, but empirical evidence for Canada is mixed: some studies show cost-effectiveness (CAD 1.30 per dollar foregone), while others find minimal effects (97 cents per dollar). Deadweight losses and tax planning distortions may offset benefits.
reforms.status_evidence: The SR&ED tax credit is described as an existing programme with established credit rates, refundability rates, and tax expenditure estimates for 2005.
reforms.importance_rationale: The SR&ED tax credit is a major, long-standing instrument of Canadian innovation policy with CAD 2.5 billion in annual tax expenditures. However, the text presents it as an existing programme rather than a new reform, and effectiveness is debated.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government provides the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Investment Tax Credit, which has the objective of encouraging the private sector to undertake scientific research and experimental development in Canada and, in particular, to assist small businesses in doing R&D.

reforms.description: The Expert Panel on Commercialization (established May 2005) recommended establishing a business-led Commercialization Partnership Board to advise the Minister of Industry and ensure private sector input into public policies for commercialisation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthens knowledge transfer from public research to market by improving coordination between government and private sector on commercialisation policy design.
reforms.status_evidence: The panel recommended the establishment of a business-led Commercialization Partnership Board; text does not confirm implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Represents a significant governance reform linking public research commercialisation to private sector priorities, though implementation status is unclear.
reforms.source_quote: The panel recommended the establishment of a business-led Commercialization Partnership Board to advise the Minister of Industry and ensure the private sector has a strong voice in the design of public policies to improve commercialisation.

reforms.description: The Expert Panel on Commercialization recommended developing a new Canada Commercialization Fellowships Program to develop talent in commercialisation and spur private sector hiring of highly qualified personnel.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Builds human capital in commercialisation skills and facilitates knowledge transfer from public research to private sector innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The panel recommended the development of a new Canada Commercialization Fellowships Program; no evidence of implementation provided.
reforms.importance_rationale: Addresses a specific gap in commercialisation talent supply, linking human capital development to knowledge transfer objectives.
reforms.source_quote: Talent: develop a new Canada Commercialization Fellowships Program; spur private sector hiring of highly qualified personnel with commercialisation talents.

reforms.description: The Expert Panel on Commercialization recommended creating a Canadian SME Partnerships Initiative to support collaborative research and commercialisation between small and medium enterprises and research institutions.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthens university-industry collaboration and knowledge transfer, particularly for SMEs that may lack internal R&D capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The panel recommended creation of a Canadian SME Partnerships Initiative; no implementation evidence provided.
reforms.importance_rationale: Addresses SME access to research and commercialisation support through structured partnerships with public research institutions.
reforms.source_quote: Research: create a Commercialization Superfund; expand federal programmes that support seed and start-up firms in proving their business ideas; and create a Canadian SME Partnerships Initiative.

reforms.description: The Expert Panel on Commercialization recommended improving access to early-stage angel financing and expertise, and identifying improvements in the expansion-stage venture capital market.
reforms.component_name: Angel financing and venture capital market improvements
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improves access to early-stage and expansion-stage capital for innovative firms, reducing financing constraints on commercialisation.
reforms.status_evidence: The panel recommended improvements to angel financing and venture capital markets; no implementation evidence provided.
reforms.importance_rationale: Targets financing gaps in the early-stage and expansion-stage venture capital markets, which are critical for scaling innovative firms.
reforms.source_quote: Capital: improve access to early-stage angel financing and expertise; identify improvements in the expansion-stage venture capital market.

reforms.description: The OECD recommends examining whether the efficiency of the SR&ED (Scientific Research and Experimental Development) tax credits might be improved, including exploring options to redesign them to target R&D in new firms and encourage incremental spending on R&D.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improved targeting of R&D tax credits toward new firms and incremental R&D spending can enhance allocative efficiency and stimulate private-sector innovation investment.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Examining whether the efficiency of the SR&ED tax credits might be improved' as a policy recommendation, indicating a proposed but not yet adopted reform.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant but targeted reform of an existing major innovation instrument (SR&ED tax credits). Redesigning the instrument to improve targeting could have meaningful effects on private R&D allocation and firm-level innovation, though the reform is still at the recommendation stage.
reforms.source_quote: Examining whether the efficiency of the SR&ED tax credits might be improved. This should include exploring the option of carefully redesigning them to target R&D in new firms and to encourage incremental spending on R&D.

reforms.description: The OECD recommends eliminating federal and provincial tax credits for investments in Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations (LSVCCs) so they compete on the same basis as other venture capital funds.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Eliminating preferential tax treatment could improve capital allocation efficiency by removing distortions, but may reduce venture capital availability if LSVCCs serve underserved markets or have lower returns.
reforms.status_evidence: Text presents this as a policy recommendation: 'Eliminating the federal and provincial tax credits for investments in Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations so that they are required to compete on the same basis as other venture capital funds.'
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant reform of the venture capital support system that would remove preferential tax treatment and level the competitive playing field. The reform addresses market distortions but is still at the recommendation stage.
reforms.source_quote: Eliminating the federal and provincial tax credits for investments in Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations so that they are required to compete on the same basis as other venture capital funds.

reforms.description: The OECD recommends developing a clearly articulated and integrated national science and technology policy with a priority-setting exercise for Canadian science, within which individual project proposals can then be assessed.
reforms.component_name: National science and technology policy framework
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: A coherent national S&T policy with clear priorities can improve the allocation of public R&D funding, reduce duplication, and align research investments with economic and social objectives.
reforms.status_evidence: Text presents this as a policy recommendation: 'Developing a clearly articulated and integrated national science and technology policy and a priority-setting exercise for Canadian science.'
reforms.importance_rationale: A structural, system-wide reform that would establish a coherent national framework for science and technology policy. This is a foundational governance reform affecting the entire public research system and the allocation of public R&D funding.
reforms.source_quote: Developing a clearly articulated and integrated national science and technology policy and a priority-setting exercise for Canadian science, within which individual project proposals can then be assessed.
